newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 8th-largest Kia Group set for bail-out.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 8th-largest Kia Group set for bail-out.

text.p: South Korea's eighth-largest conglomerate, the Kia Group, has been designated for a bail-out, a central Bank of Korea spokesman said on Tuesday.
Creditor banks to the group, whose flagship unit is Kia Motors Corp, are due to officially announce details at 0530 GMT, the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
The group's main creditor, the Korea First Bank, confirmed there would be an official announcement on the bail-out decision but declined to give details.
Kia has been troubled by worsening cash flow problems because financial institutions, alarmed by two major corporate collapses earlier this year, have tightened credit lines.
An official at the Kia Group's public information department declined to comment on the news of the bail-out.
South Korean financial markets have been rocked by the collapse under heavy debt of Hanbo Steel Co in January, followed in March by Sammi Steel Co.
In April domestic financial institutions formed a voluntary committee to keep promising companies from going bankrupt in an effort to break a chain of corporate failures.
The Kia Group had total liabilities of 11.89 trillion won at the end of 1996, more than five times its shareholders' equity of 2.27 trillion won, Bank of Korea statistics showed.
The statistics also showed the group ran a combined net loss of 129.4 billion won on 12.1 trillion won in sales in 1996.
So far, the Jinro and Dainong groups had been selected for bail-out by the voluntary committee.
